newsitem.title: USA: CVS shareholders, FTC approve $2.8 billion Revco deal.
newsitem.headline: CVS shareholders, FTC approve $2.8 billion Revco deal.

text.p: CVS Corp. said Tuesday its shareholders approved the company's $2.8 billion acquisition of Revco D.S. Inc., which will create the nation's largest drugstore chain.

The deal, which would make CVS the industry leader based on store locations, will be voted separately by Revco shareholders Wednesday. CVS also said it reached a preliminary agreement with the Federal Trade Commission on the deal.
After the announcement, Revco's stock climbed $1.25 to $42.125 and CVS added the same amount to $47.875, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
In February, CVS said it would acquire Twinsburg, Ohio-based Revco for stock worth $2.8 billion and assume $900 million of debt.

Revco, which operates nearly 2,600 stores in Midwestern, Southeastern and Eastern states, posted $5.4 billion in sales in 1996. CVS, with 1,425 stores in 14 states and the District of Columbia, has a strong presence in the Northeast and the mid-Atlantic regions.

CVS said it and FTC staff agreed on terms of a consent decree, which if approved by the commission, allow it to move forward with the merger. It said the agreement was now being considered by the full commission and that a decision was expected shortly.
